{{Draft}}
<translate>
<!--T:1-->
The '''directory''' is the single register of every person, organisation and institution that appears anywhere in openCR: collectors and owners, galleries and dealers, museums and foundations, auction houses, printers and foundries, publishers, photographers, authors, curators, sponsors and lenders. Every other entity points to it: an artwork's owners and agents, a publication's authors, an event's organisers, an artist's gallerist.

<!--T:2-->
The directory is shared by all catalogues. A museum holding works by several artists exists only once. This page explains how directory entries are recorded and how to control what the public sees of them. For the list of sections, see [[How openCR is structured/Records and their sections#Directory|Records and their sections]]; for every single field, see the [[Field reference]].

<!--T:3-->
== Before creating an entry ==
* '''Search first.''' The person or institution may already exist, entered for another artist. Duplicates split the information about one owner or gallery across two records.
* '''Choose the short name carefully.''' The ''Alias'' is what appears in every list where a directory entry can be picked, and the directory is picked everywhere. Make it unique and recognisable. A renamed alias changes in every list at once, which is correct but can surprise others who work with the entry.

<!--T:4-->
== The main record ==
The main data of a directory entry are edited in a pop-up: in ''Edit Mode'', the pencil at the start of the entry opens ''Main record of the entry''. ''Type'', ''Name 1'' and ''Alias'' are required.
* '''Type''': ''Person'', ''Private organization'' or ''Public organization''.
* '''Public (shown on open.cr)''': publishes the entry. Leave it unticked until it is complete.
* '''Name 1''' and '''Name 2''': for a person, typically first name and surname; for an organisation, the full name in ''Name 1'', with ''Name 2'' left empty.
* '''Alias''': the short name (see above). When another entry already has the same alias, the pop-up refuses it, and names the other entry if you may see it.
* The three privacy ticks described [[#What the public sees|below]].
Internal remarks go into private notes in the entry's ''Notes'' block (see [[Objects#Notes|notes]]). The bin after the main record deletes the entry (see [[#Shared between catalogues|below]]).

<!--T:5-->
New entries are created with '''Easy directory creation''' in the ''PRO menu'', or, in ''Edit Mode'', with the plus icon at the top of an entry's page, which opens the same form in a new tab. The form asks for the type, the names and the alias, a first address, the privacy ticks, up to two activities and a phone number, mobile number, website and email address; the type, ''Name1'', the alias and the first activity are required. When you choose the type, the form sets the ticks: for a person, ''Public'' is unticked and the three privacy ticks are ticked, so ownership histories and sales keep the person's name hidden even after ''Public'' is ticked; for an organisation, ''Public'' is ticked and the three privacy ticks are unticked. Check them before saving. The first address is public when the entry is. The form does not check whether the alias is already taken, so search first. The new entry is linked to the artist's catalogue (see [[#Shared between catalogues|below]]).

<!--T:6-->
== Sections ==
In ''Edit Mode'', the plus icon next to a section's heading opens a pop-up for a new entry, the pencil before an entry opens it, and the bin after it deletes it.
* '''Contact details''': phone, mobile, fax, email, website, social media and others. Each contact has its own ''Public'' tick, so a public website and a private phone number can sit side by side. A new contact of a person starts unticked, one of an organisation ticked. Email addresses and web addresses are checked, and the same contact cannot be entered twice.
* '''Activities''': what the entry does. The list mixes roles of people with kinds of institutions: Gallery, Publisher, Photographer, Curator, Printer, Writer, Museum, Auction house, Foundry, Foundation, University and many more. An entry can have several activities, for example both ''Gallery'' and ''Publisher'', each of them once. An optional comment is shown in ''Edit Mode'' only. Activities have no ''Public'' tick; they are always shown.
* '''Related persons and organizations''': links to other directory entries: works for, is member of, is founder of, is owner of, is sponsor of, is teacher of, is colleague of, is successor of, has taken over, has absorbed, is related (family), knows and others. The pop-up searches the other entry by name or alias, and shows how both pages will read the link. A relation can carry the period during which it existed, from and to, each with day, month, year and a qualifier; years before Christ are possible. ''Show on public pages'' publishes the relation; it is ticked by itself when both entries are public. Enter each relation once; the reverse direction (such as ''is student of'' for ''is teacher of'') is shown automatically, and the pop-up refuses the same relation with the same dates a second time, from either side. The same relation for another period is allowed.
* '''Related events''': the events in which the entry takes part, each with its role, such as organiser, curator or exhibiting gallery. The pop-up ''Add to an event'' searches the events you may edit; a role can be limited to one place of a touring exhibition. It is the same list as ''Related agents'' on the [[Events|event]]. The public view lists only public events.
* '''Description''', '''Sources''' and '''Notes''': a text about the entry, where the information comes from, and remarks (see [[Sources and citations]]).

<!--T:7-->
The page also shows where the entry appears in other records. These lists are changed in those records, not here:
* ''Relations with Artist'': the artists' relations to the entry, entered on the [[Artists#Contacts, relations and collections|artist's page]];
* ''Publications (as publisher)'' and ''Publications (as author)'': the publications the entry published or wrote, entered in the publication's ''Agents'';
* ''Artists in the collection'': the artists whose works the entry holds as a collection (it cannot be changed on the editing pages at present);
* ''Objects in property'': the works the entry owns or owned, from their ownership histories;
* ''Agent'': the works in which the entry was involved, by role, from their ''Agents'';
* ''Named on works'': the works whose marks and inscriptions name the entry, for example in a dedication.

<!--T:8-->
== Addresses ==
An entry can have several addresses, and they change over time, so they have a page of their own, '''Addresses'''. On the entry's page, in ''Edit Mode'', ''Address'' leads there: with a plus sign while the entry has no address, with a pencil once it has one. The page lists the addresses: the plus sign after ''Addresses'' adds one, the pencil before an address opens it in a pop-up, and the bin after it deletes it. Each address has:
* a type: Legal address, Mailing / Correspondence, Residence, Studio / Atelier, Office / Administration, Exhibition space / Showroom, Workshop / Production, or Storage / Depot;
* the address lines, street, ZIP code, city, state and country. At least one of them must be filled in; none is required on its own;
* a period of validity (from and to, each with a qualifier) and a note on the period;
* a comment;
* '''Primary address (shown by default)''': the main address of the entry, the one its page shows. Lists of directory entries show its city and country. The first address of an entry is its primary address, and it stays primary until another address is ticked as primary. When the primary address is deleted, the first current address takes its place;
* '''Currently valid''': whether the address is still current. The list marks the others as ''Not current'';
* its own '''Public''' tick, so an address can be recorded without being published;
* its sources and notes (see [[Sources and citations]]). Once an address is saved, its pop-up has ''Add source'' buttons for the street, the ZIP code, the city and the country, and one for the address as a whole; notes are added in the same way. The primary address can also be cited on the entry's page.

<!--T:9-->
== What the public sees ==
The directory holds sensitive information: who owns what, who bought what and for how much. Several settings work together:

<!--T:10-->
{| class="wikitable"
! Setting !! Effect
|-
| '''Public (shown on open.cr)''' || Unticked: open.cr does not show the entry's page, and public pages show ''Private collection'', ''Transactions are private'' or ''private data'' instead of its name. In the editors' view, the editors of the catalogues it is linked to see it.
|-
| '''Collection private''' || The entry's public page does not show the list ''Artists in the collection'', and the entry is not named as the recipient of a dedication.
|-
| '''Provenance private''' || Where the entry owns or owned a work, the ownership history shows ''Private collection'' instead of its name. Its public page does not show its ''Objects in property'', and the entry is not named as the recipient of a dedication.
|-
| '''Transactions private''' || Where the entry sold or bought a work, or acted as intermediary, the sale shows ''Transactions are private'' instead of its name.
|-
| ''Public'' of single entries || Contact details, addresses and relations can be hidden one by one; so can a single entry of an artwork's ownership history.
|}

<!--T:11-->
The settings can be combined freely. A typical case: a collector agrees to be named as the owner of works, but not to have their purchases published. Then the entry is public, while ''Transactions private'' is ticked.

<!--T:12-->
The privacy ticks work across all artworks at once. To hide just one entry of one artwork's ownership history, untick ''Show on public pages'' on that entry instead.

<!--T:13-->
== Shared between catalogues ==
Because the directory is shared, an entry can be used in several artists' catalogues: any catalogue can use a public entry. An entry can also be linked to artists' catalogues. The editors of a linked catalogue may edit the entry, and see and use it even while it is not public; for any other entry, ask the platform administrator. ''Easy directory creation'' links a new entry to the artist it is created for. On the page ''Address Book'' in the ''PRO menu'', a public entry of a private or public organisation whose primary address has a country can be linked to the artist's catalogue with ''Link'', or unlinked with ''Unlink''; persons and entries that are not public are not listed there.
* This link is not a relationship. To record that a gallery represents an artist, add a relation on the [[Artists#Contacts, relations and collections|artist's page]] instead.

<!--T:14-->
Changes to a shared entry show up in every catalogue that uses it. Entries used by several artists' catalogues can only be deleted by someone with editing rights for all of them; in practice, ask the platform administrator. An entry cannot be deleted while other records still refer to it, for example an ownership history, an event or a publication; remove those links first.

<!--T:15-->
== Before publishing ==
* Type, names and alias are complete.
* Activities are recorded.
* The privacy ticks match what the person or institution has agreed to.
* Only contact details, addresses and relations that may be public are ticked ''Public'' or ''Show on public pages''.
Then tick ''Public (shown on open.cr)'' in the main record.

<!--T:16-->
== Common pitfalls ==
* '''Duplicates.''' Search before creating; the entry may exist for another artist.
* '''Owner shown as a private collection.''' When an owner unexpectedly appears as ''Private collection'', or a seller as ''Transactions are private'', check ''Public (shown on open.cr)'' and the privacy ticks in the entry's main record.
* '''Catalogue link used as a relationship.''' A gallerist, publisher or collector of an artist is recorded in the artist's relations with the directory; linking the entry to the artist's catalogue only lets the artist's editors edit and use it, and says nothing about their relationship.
* '''Mirror relations.''' A relation between two directory entries is entered once.
* '''The artist as a directory entry.''' When the artist themselves owned a work or performed an action, use the tick for the artist in that entry (see [[Objects#People and history|Objects]]) instead of creating a directory entry for the artist.
